star-order.why: Situation and task set up the story briefly; the action is the core; the result closes it. A short reflection after the result often helps.

where-time.why: Interviewers assess your judgement and behaviour, which live in the action. Keep the setup short.

i-vs-we.why: The interviewer is hiring you, so they need your part. Be specific about your actions without taking credit for others' work.

no-metric.why: Invented numbers are fabrication and tend to collapse under follow-up questions. A true qualitative result is stronger than a made-up metric.

failure-question.why: Interviewers look for ownership and learning. A real mistake with a clear fix and change in behaviour shows both.

disagreement.why: The behaviour is the point: respectful challenge with data, openness to being wrong, and commitment to the outcome.

reuse-stories.why: A good story about a hard project might show ownership, prioritisation and conflict. Six to eight strong stories cover most interviews.

long-is-better.why: Most strong answers take 1 to 3 minutes. Long setups crowd out the action and lose the interviewer; they'll ask follow-ups for detail.
